[[File:Ben Lacey DecipherCon 1999.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Ben Lacey at DecipherCon 1999. Photo: Decipher.]]
'''Ben Lacey''' of Franklin, Tennessee, is a [[Star Trek CCG]] player. He qualified for the 1999 Star Trek CCG World Championship at [[DecipherCon 1999]] by winning the Atlanta Open, and finished third.<ref name="st-finalists">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/stworldchamp/finalists.html Meet the 1999 Star Trek CCG World Championship Finalists], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011005154442/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/stworldchamp/finalists.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="st-final12">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/stworldchamp/final12.html Meet the 1999 Star Trek CCG World Championship Final 12], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122121259/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/stworldchamp/final12.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decipher's DecipherCon caption called him one half of the Lacey gang.<ref name="sat49">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/SAT/sat49.html DecipherCon 1999 Saturday photo sat49], Decipher (1999). Caption: "Ben Lacey, one half of the Lacey gang, the tough crew from Franklin, Tennessee". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001025142504/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/SAT/sat49.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Star Trek CCG ==

Lacey entered the 1999 Star Trek CCG World Championship as one of 32 finalists, with a rating of 1794.<ref name="st-finalists" /> He finished the eight-game preliminary round third at 11 (149). He lost his first game to [[James Monsebroten]].<ref name="st02">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/ST02_1.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: 1999 ST World Championships], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001031210057/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/ST02_1.html Internet Archive]</ref> In the four-game Round of 12 he scored 6 (110) and again placed third; the top two met in the final.<ref name="st03">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/ST03_1.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: ST World Championships], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001219092400/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/ST03_1.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="st-final12" />

Lacey was disqualified from the Star Trek CCG event at the 2000 World Championships in Orlando, Florida, the weekend of the [[2000 Decipher World Championship]]. His deck held four copies of a card that his decklist gave as three. [[Steven Lewis]] reported it and called him a good friend from Nashville.<ref name="lewis">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-15-how-to-get-disqualified-at-worldsd1349/ how-to-get-disqualified-at-worlds], Steven Lewis, Decktech (15 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024010428/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-15-how-to-get-disqualified-at-worldsd1349/ Internet Archive]</ref>
